metadata.title: Stage Runner: Inside the Godot Code
metadata.audience: makers following the channel's Claude + Walker game workflows
metadata.note: godot-gamedev walker film. Code panels are Godot editor reconstructions with verbatim source; each is followed by real engine output of the same build. No game change, no paid calls, no upload.

beats.narration_text: Hola, this is Liam, in for Bear. That's the kind of prompt Walker expects, reconstructed here, not a transcript. This time we open the project itself: a piece of code, then the exact thing it does on screen, in the real build.

props.command: Please use Walker to convert my game design document about a vertical shooter — fly a wisp up three ruined city streets, shoot the monster army marching down at you, and defeat the Cerberus at the city gate — into a playable Godot project.
props.runningText: illustrative reconstruction — not the historical prompt
output: Built: 7 thin scenes, 14 scripts and a shader, 2,210 lines.
Art from the Unity folder; sound synthesized.

beats.narration_text: Stage Runner is built in code. Its seven scene files are a few lines each, and twenty-two hundred lines of GDScript build every street, monster and menu at runtime. So every piece of code we read has a result you can watch.

props.text:
Stage Runner
is built from scenes.
Seven scene files, a few lines each,
and 2,210 lines of GDScript
that build every street.

qc.sparse_reason: Hesitant writer: text is typed on screen over the narration, so mid-beat samples legitimately show a partial page. The finished text fills the safe area and holds for the last 1.5 s.

beats.narration_text: Open a stage scene and there's one node. Run it for eight seconds, and game dot g d has built the rest: a background with two copies of the street painting, a world holding the player and the first monsters, a camera for screen shake, and two canvas layers, one for the HUD and one for the banner and menus. A hundred and thirteen nodes.

props.title: Saved Scene vs. Live Tree
props.source: Live tree: printed from a running instance of res://scenes/stage_1.tscn at 8 s, headless, no input, on an isolated copy (tree_probe.gd).

beats.narration_text: Here's the whole of stage one: seven lines. One Node2D, with game dot g d attached, and a single property, stage I D, set to one. Stages two and three are the same file with a different number. Everything else is built when the scene starts.

beats.narration_text: Movement reads the four move actions as one vector, so diagonals aren't faster. Holding focus halves the speed. Then the position clamps to the street, not to the screen, which is where Unity clamped.

props.title: Move, Focus, Clamp
props.source: scripts/player.gd:95-102 at d90fa19 · Godot editor reconstruction
props.code:
move = Input.get_vector("move_left", "move_right", "move_up", "move_down")
			wants_fire = Input.is_action_pressed("fire")
			focus = Input.is_action_pressed("focus")
	var speed := MOVE_SPEED * (FOCUS_FACTOR if focus else 1.0)
	position += move.limit_length(1.0) * speed * delta
	# MainChar clamps to the camera bounds; here the bounds are the playfield.
	position.x = clampf(position.x, field.position.x + 28, field.end.x - 28)
	position.y = clampf(position.y, field.position.y + 34, field.end.y - 30)

beats.narration_text: Shift held: half speed, the hitbox dot appears, and the wisp stays inside the street.

beats.narration_text: A shot is a list of angles. Normally it's one angle, straight up. While spread time is above zero, it's three: minus point two, zero, and plus point two radians. Each bullet's velocity is straight up, rotated by its angle.

props.title: One Shot Becomes Three
props.source: scripts/player.gd:122-131 at d90fa19 · Godot editor reconstruction

beats.narration_text: A triple-shot pickup sets spread time to ten seconds, and every shot fans into three.

beats.narration_text: Every monster walks down, like Unity's. Then the pattern adds one thing. Weave sways seventy pixels either way. Hunt drifts toward the player's column until it passes them. Hop only squashes the sprite as it walks.

props.title: Four Ways to Walk Down
props.source: scripts/enemy.gd:96-108 at d90fa19 · Godot editor reconstruction
props.code:
position.y += speed * delta
	match pattern:
		"weave":
			position.x = base_x + sin(age * 2.4 + phase) * 70.0
		"hunt":
			if is_instance_valid(target) and target.visible and position.y < target.position.y:
				base_x = move_toward(base_x, target.position.x, 70.0 * delta)
			position.x = base_x
			sprite.flip_h = target != null and is_instance_valid(target) and target.position.x > position.x
		"hop":
			var squash := sin(age * 6.0 + phase)
			sprite.scale = Vector2(1.0 + squash * 0.08, 1.0 - squash * 0.08)
	position.x = clampf(position.x, field.position.x + 30, field.end.x - 30)

beats.narration_text: When a kill rolls a drop, this decides what it is. It's a heart only if a life is missing, and then forty percent of the time. Otherwise it's a triple shot. At full health, a heart can never drop.

beats.narration_text: Game over keeps Unity's idea, as the comment says: show the screen, and stop the game. The text is the score against the goal, or, in the boss stage, a line about the Cerberus. Then the menu shows and the whole tree pauses.

beats.narration_text: Clearing a stage is one tween. It pops the banner, waits, flies the wisp off the top of the street, then records the stage's score and loads the next scene: the clear card, or after stage three, the credits. The comments name Unity's scenes.

props.title: Stage Clear Is One Tween
props.source: scripts/game.gd:579-591 at d90fa19 · Godot editor reconstruction
props.code:
banner.scale = Vector2(0.4, 0.4)
	var tween := create_tween()
	tween.tween_property(banner, "scale", Vector2.ONE, 0.45).set_trans(Tween.TRANS_BACK).set_ease(Tween.EASE_OUT)
	tween.tween_interval(0.6)
	# The wisp runs off the top of the screen toward the next stage.
	tween.tween_property(player, "position:y", -80.0, 1.1).set_trans(Tween.TRANS_QUAD).set_ease(Tween.EASE_IN)
	tween.tween_interval(0.4)
	tween.tween_callback(func():
		GameState.complete_stage(stage_id, score, kills)
		if stage_id >= GameState.STAGE_COUNT:
			GameState.go_to("game_clear")   # GameManager: SceneManager.LoadScene("ClearTheGame")
		else:
			GameState.go_to("stage_clear"))  # GameManager: SceneManager.LoadScene("FinishStageOne")

beats.narration_text: The boss counts its attacks and takes the count modulo four. Zero and two fire an aimed fan, one fires a ring, and three summons two minions, unless the street already holds four monsters, in which case it fires a tight three-shot fan.

props.title: Four Attacks in a Loop
props.source: scripts/boss.gd:94-106 at d90fa19 · Godot editor reconstruction
props.code:
func _attack() -> void:
	match attack_index % 4:
		0, 2:
			_fan(7 if enraged() else 5, 0.95 if enraged() else 0.7, 220.0)
		1:
			_ring(16 if enraged() else 12, 160.0)
		3:
			if get_tree().get_nodes_in_group("enemies").size() < 4:
				summon.emit([position + Vector2(-120, 30), position + Vector2(120, 30)])
				Audio.play("boss_roar", -8.0)
			else:
				_fan(3, 0.3, 300.0)
	attack_index += 1

beats.narration_text: Fan, ring, fan, and two minions drop in beside it.

beats.narration_text: Damage first checks the state. While it's walking in, the shot is absorbed: a spark, but no damage. After that, it loses health. The moment it crosses half, it tints red, roars, and attacks again almost at once.

beats.narration_text: There's no input map in the project settings. The GameState autoload builds it at startup: W A S D and the arrows, J, Space and Z to fire, the left mouse button too, then the gamepad: A to fire, the left bumper to focus, Start to pause.

props.title: The Input Map Is Code
props.source: scripts/game_state.gd:122-136 at d90fa19 · Godot editor reconstruction
props.code:
func _configure_input() -> void:
	_add_keys("move_left", [KEY_A, KEY_LEFT])
	_add_keys("move_right", [KEY_D, KEY_RIGHT])
	_add_keys("move_up", [KEY_W, KEY_UP])
	_add_keys("move_down", [KEY_S, KEY_DOWN])
	_add_keys("fire", [KEY_J, KEY_SPACE, KEY_Z])
	_add_keys("focus", [KEY_SHIFT])
	_add_keys("pause", [KEY_ESCAPE, KEY_P])
	_add_keys("restart", [KEY_R])
	_add_mouse("fire", MOUSE_BUTTON_LEFT)

	_add_joy_button("fire", JOY_BUTTON_A)
	_add_joy_button("focus", JOY_BUTTON_LEFT_SHOULDER)
	_add_joy_button("pause", JOY_BUTTON_START)
	_add_joy_axis("fire", JOY_AXIS_TRIGGER_RIGHT, 1.0)

beats.narration_text: Here's the defect. Pause toggles the menu and marks the event handled. Restart does the same, but restart changes the scene first. By the next line, this node has left the tree, its viewport is null, and the call fails.

beats.narration_text: The rest of the project, in one pass. A main menu with the best score and an audio button, and a How to Play page. An audio autoload with fifteen sounds and three music loops, all synthesized by a Python tool. And a playtest that clears all three stages, steering through a hook the player script exposes for it. The film's captures pressed the keys instead.

beats.narration_text: Verdict. This is a small project you can read top to bottom: thin scenes, one stage script driven by a table, and a boss in under two hundred lines. One real defect: R on a menu logs a script error, one line too late. Its own test steers through a hook; the captures pressed keys. And nobody has played it yet.

artifactLines: Implemented: 7 thin scenes; game.gd builds each stage from the STAGES table.
Good habits: one damage per bullet; a mercy rule; hearts only when a life is missing.
Defect: R on the pause menu logs a SCRIPT ERROR at game.gd:606; restart still works.
Not judged: fun, difficulty, boss fairness. 0 human playtests.
